extracted.intended_audience: Authors/researchers reporting system-level healthcare quality improvement projects
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and structuring manuscripts that report system-level initiatives to improve quality, safety, value, and related outcomes in healthcare, including methods to establish that observed outcomes were due to the intervention(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate that the manuscript concerns an initiative to improve healthcare (broadly defined to include the quality, safety, effectiveness, patient-centeredness, timeliness, cost, efficiency, and equity of healthcare).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear in the title that the report concerns a quality improvement initiative; the term 'initiative' (or equivalent) should signal the manuscript's QI focus and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide adequate information to aid in searching and indexing; summarize all key information from various sections of the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the abstract format of the intended publication or a structured summary such as: background, local problem, methods, interventions, results, conclusions. Ensure sufficient detail to enable discoverability and accurate indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem Description
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature and significance of the local problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the project was started; describe the specific local problem being addressed and why it matters in that setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available Knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of what is currently known about the problem, including relevant previous studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situate the work within existing literature and evidence; summarize prior findings that informed the project and highlight gaps the project aims to address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal or formal frameworks, models, concepts, and/or theories used to explain the problem, any reasons or assumptions that were used to develop the intervention(s), and reasons why the intervention(s) was expected to work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the conceptual or theoretical basis for the intervention(s), including assumptions and mechanisms by which the intervention was hypothesized to produce change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose of the project and of this report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state the aims and objectives of the project and what the manuscript intends to communicate or demonstrate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextual elements considered important at the outset of introducing the intervention(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the setting, organizational, cultural, and other contextual factors anticipated to influence implementation and outcomes; note which contextual elements were considered when planning the intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the intervention(s) in sufficient detail that others could reproduce it; specifics of the team involved in the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough detail about the intervention components, timeline, and delivery so others can reproduce it. Describe team composition, roles, and responsibilities for implementing the intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study of the Intervention(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach chosen for assessing the impact of the intervention(s); approach used to establish whether the observed outcomes were due to the intervention(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain study design or evaluation approach (e.g., time-series, controlled comparisons, qualitative evaluation) and methods used to attribute observed changes to the intervention rather than other causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures chosen for studying processes and outcomes of the intervention(s), including rationale for choosing them, their operational definitions, and their validity and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also describe the approach to ongoing assessment of contextual elements that contributed to success, failure, efficiency, and cost, and the methods employed for assessing completeness and accuracy of data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative and quantitative methods used to draw inferences from the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe analytic techniques used (statistical tests, time-series analysis, qualitative approaches) and methods for understanding variation within the data, including the effects of time as a variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical aspects of implementing and studying the intervention(s) and how they were addressed, including, but not limited to, formal ethics review and potential conflict(s) of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report approvals, consent procedures (if any), privacy protections, and how conflicts of interest were managed; discuss ethical trade-offs of the intervention and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results
rubrics_metrics.description: What was found regarding the intervention(s), processes, outcomes, context, and unintended consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: (a) initial steps of the intervention(s) and their evolution over time (e.g., time-line diagram, flow chart, or table), including modifications made during the project; (b) details of the process measures and outcome; (c) contextual elements that interacted with the intervention(s); (d) observed associations between outcomes, interventions, and relevant contextual elements; (e) unintended consequences such as unexpected benefits, problems, failures, or costs associated with the intervention(s); (f) details about missing data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Key findings, including relevance to the rationale and specific aims; particular strengths of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise synthesis of main results and why they matter in relation to stated aims and underlying rationale; highlight notable strengths or successes of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation of findings, including the nature of the association between the intervention(s) and the outcomes, comparisons with other work, and impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address: (a) nature of the association between the intervention(s) and the outcomes; (b) comparison of results with findings from other publications; (c) impact of the project on people and systems; (d) reasons for any differences between observed and anticipated outcomes, including the influence of context; (e) costs and strategic trade-offs, including opportunity costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits to the generalizability of the work and factors that might have limited internal validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss limits such as confounding, bias, imprecision in design, methods, measurement, or analysis, and describe efforts made to minimize and adjust for these limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions about the usefulness, sustainability, and potential spread of the work, and implications for practice and further study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address: (a) usefulness of the work; (b) sustainability; (c) potential for spread to other contexts; (d) implications for practice and for further study in the field; (e) suggested next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources of funding that supported this work and the role, if any, of the funding organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report funding sources and explicitly state the role of funders in design, implementation, interpretation, and reporting of the project.
